Keep the storefront, add the voice: Some accounts are never going to browse a catalog. They will talk instead, at the end of a shift, from the walk-in. The storefront stays for the ones who tap, and VOS picks up the ones who talk.

Try it on the accounts still phoning: VOS goes in beside what you run without a rollout, so you can put it on the handful of accounts that never adopted and judge it on those before you decide anything bigger.

The ERP keeps being the one destination: Both feed the system you have, so adding VOS does not change where an order ends up. It arrives over EDI, the API or QuickBooks, into the same place your people already work.

@graph.name: Is VOS a true Pepper alternative, and is it better than Pepper?

acceptedAnswer.text: Those have the same answer: it depends what you are fixing. If the goal is to get orders off the phone and into something structured, VOS does that job, your customers approve each line themselves, and getting started does not take a quarter. If the goal is one platform running your storefront, your reps, your collections and your pricing, Pepper is built wide for that and VOS is not. We would rather say so now than at the demo.

@graph.name: How quickly can we actually be taking orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most distributors reach that point in a day or two. There is no IT project here, and nothing to pull out of your stack, which is the main reason a Pepper alternative gets shortlisted at all. Pepper's own published window is a good deal longer, which is fair for how much it is standing up.

@graph.name: Do we have to drop Pepper to bring VOS in?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. VOS is additive by design and runs beside what you already have, so nothing needs switching off to try it. If you have an ERP you like and a storefront you are keeping, VOS covers how the order arrives and leaves both in place.

@graph.name: Will VOS replace our ERP or order management system?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, it does not. VOS is the way in: it gets the order from your customer to you, confirmed and itemized. From there it reaches your existing software or your inbox, and how you pick, bill and ship does not change.
We quote by distributor, so tell us about your operation and we will price it. Pepper quotes too, and publishes no rate card either, so a demo on both sides is the only way to compare the two fairly.

@graph.name: Do our customers need new hardware or a tablet?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. VOS works on the iOS or Android phone that is already in their pocket. We send nothing out, there is nothing to bolt to a counter, and no device for you to support.

@graph.name: What happens to the customers who still call their order in?

acceptedAnswer.text: They can keep phoning, and your team handles those exactly as it does now. Worth being clear though: a call or a voicemail does not get a VOS order number, a timestamp or a stock movement. Only what comes through the app does.

@graph.name: Where do the Pepper details on this page come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pepper's own website. The module list, the storefront and Order Agent descriptions and the implementation window were all read off usepepper.com on 10 October 2026, including their own post on how long an implementation takes. We have not repeated their marketing numbers here. If any of it has changed since, this page is the thing that is out of date, not them.
